why: Daniel 1:3 speaks of the Israelites, the people, not the patriarch Israel (Jacob) whom Bible Atlas links.

Many Christians read the one like a son of man in 7:13-14 as Jesus, and many Jewish readers see Israel or an angelic figure, but the chapter does not name him; the readings are set out in the chapter's notes.
Many Christians read the anointed one in 9:25-26 as Jesus, while others point to Cyrus, a high priest or a later ruler; the text does not name him, and the readings are in the chapter's notes.

Bible Atlas links the Ahasuerus of Esther, who is Xerxes I (reigned 486-465 BC). Daniel 9:1 names the father of Darius the Mede, a different and otherwise unknown man, so this link would send readers to the wrong king.
Bible Atlas draws Uphaz in central India, but no one knows where the gold of Uphaz came from (some think it is a variant spelling of Ophir). The map shows no dot.
In 11:41 Edom and Moab mean the nations and their lands, which are already linked as places, not the patriarch Esau or Lot's son Moab.
